Training

Home workout for beginners with no equipment

You do not need a gym membership to get stronger and lose fat. This plan needs a floor, a wall and a sturdy chair, fits in a two-metre square and takes about 30 minutes, three days a week.

By Khushi Gupta · Reviewed October 2026 · 3 min read

On this page

  1. How the plan works
  2. The workout
  3. How to progress
  4. Add walking for fat loss

How the plan works

Do the workout three days a week with a rest day between, for example Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Each session trains the whole body. Rest 60 to 90 seconds between sets.

Early morning or late evening avoids the worst of the summer heat. Keep a fan on and water nearby: you will sweat more than you expect.

The workout

ExerciseSets x repsEasier version
Bodyweight squat3 x 12-15Squat to a chair
Push-up3 x 6-12Hands on a wall or table
Reverse lunge3 x 8 each legHold a wall for balance
Glute bridge3 x 12-15Smaller range
Chair dip2 x 6-10Bend knees, feet closer
Plank3 x 20-40 sKnees down
Superman hold2 x 20 sLift arms only

Start with a 5-minute warm-up: marching on the spot, arm circles and 10 slow squats. Finish with a few minutes of stretching.

Advertisements

How to progress

The body adapts to what you do, so the workout has to get slightly harder every week or two. This is progressive overload, and it is what makes a home workout keep working.

  • Add 1 or 2 reps per set until you reach the top of the range.
  • Then move to a harder version: wall push-ups to table push-ups to floor push-ups.
  • Slow the lowering part to 3 seconds to make a set harder.
  • After 6 to 8 weeks, add a fourth set or a fourth day.
  • When bodyweight gets easy, a pair of adjustable dumbbells opens up the home dumbbell workout.

Add walking for fat loss

If fat loss is your goal, the workout keeps your muscle while your diet does most of the work. A 30 to 45 minute walk on the other days burns an extra 150 to 250 kcal. The calories burned calculator shows what each activity burns at your weight, and the Indian diet plan for weight loss covers the food side.

Frequently asked questions

Can I build muscle with home workouts?

Yes, especially as a beginner. As long as each set is taken close to failure and you progress to harder versions, bodyweight training builds muscle. Progress slows after a year or so without added weight.

How long before I see results from home workouts?

Most people feel stronger in 2 to 3 weeks and see visible changes in 6 to 10 weeks, if they train three times a week and eat to match their goal.

Is 30 minutes of exercise a day enough?

Yes. Three 30-minute strength sessions a week plus daily walking meets the WHO activity guidelines for adults.

Should I work out every day?

Not with this plan. Muscles need a day to recover between full-body sessions. Walk, stretch or play a sport on the rest days.
